plan.topic: Left your tirzepatide pen out of the fridge? What the US label and Instructions for Use say about storage, and what to do if you're unsure.
plan.angle:
08:00 practical-moment 'Is this normal / is it OK?' Short, tight arm (90–120 words).

- **Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer):** 'Left your tirzepatide pen out of the fridge? Here's what the label says.'
- **By 6 s:** the label's unrefrigerated-storage wording, with its exact temperature and day limits. Copy them from the current Zepbound PI (rev. 28 Aug 2026) and the single-dose pen IFU, each with its own URL. Quote only if the IFU loads.
- **Other label storage lines:** don't freeze, and don't use a pen that has been frozen. Protect it from light, as the label prints it.
- **Scope:** the US single-dose pen. KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets, and UK and Australian packs may differ, so check the leaflet in your box.
- **Untagged line:** if you're not sure whether a pen is still OK, ask your pharmacist before using it.
- **Leave out:** dose amounts, missed-dose talk, travel dates and holiday words.
- **Closing:** the scoped don't-stop/change line, then 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. Exp F is still running, so the Exp F line goes second to last.
- **Post note:** the related-video target is the Pen how-to long video (11-11).

package.title: Tirzepatide Pen Left Out of the Fridge? #shorts
package.description:
A tirzepatide pen left out of the fridge isn't automatically ruined. The US label for the single-dose pen allows up to 21 days unrefrigerated, at or below 30°C/86°F. Never use a frozen pen. Check the leaflet in your box, and if you're unsure, ask your pharmacist before using it.
Don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#tirzepatide #GLP1 #shorts
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta: Spoken close (Exp F, 08:00 slot): "We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps. Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description." POST NOTE for owner: set the Studio related-video link to the Pen how-to long video (11-11). Word count: 120 spoken words by my own count (tight arm, 90–120), about 48–50 s. Fact-check fixes applied: (1) the s1 card now names tirzepatide; (2) the s2 card carries the scope (US label, single-dose pen, unrefrigerated), and the narration says "30 degrees Celsius"; (3) s5 list item 2 now reads "KwikPens and multi-dose vials: different limits". Sources now use the fact-checker's verified HTML label URLs. Source note: the single-dose pen Instructions for Use couldn't be loaded, so nothing is quoted. All storage lines are paraphrased and tagged to PI section 16.2 only. The pharmacist line and the safety lines are our own and carry no tag.

factcheck.summary: Every storage claim matches US label section 16.2, and the script is safe to ship. I checked it against Lilly's HTML versions of both labels (Zepbound and Mounjaro, both revised August 2026), because the cited PDF files exist but couldn't be read as text. Both labels say a single-dose pen can be kept unrefrigerated at up to 30°C (86°F) for up to 21 days. Both say don't freeze it, don't use it if it has been frozen, and store it in the original carton to protect it from light. The Mounjaro label also says to throw it away after 21 days at room temperature. The scope line is accurate: KwikPens and multi-dose vials have different limits (28 or 30 days after first use), and UK and Australian packs may differ. My count is 117 spoken words, inside the tight 90–120 arm. The safety close, the Exp F line and the closing line are in the right order and word for word. There's no dosing, no switching advice and no unsupported claim. The hook delivers on its promise, because the two limits come right after it and the pharmacist line covers the 'unsure' case. Three minor fixes are listed below (opening card, stat card, list card).
